reason: Split into 6 functional cases for the summary endpoint's sort parameter (count order with name ties, name, default, unknown/empty/case-variant 400) and 7 e2e cases for the Brands page Sort control (initial state, choosing Most products, reload, direct link, unknown and case-variant fallback, switching back).

items.title: Summary with sort=count orders brands by item count descending, ties by name
covers: AC4: sort=count orders by number of products, largest first
AC2: brands with the same number in alphabetical order
items.reason: AC4 requires the API to order by number of products when `sort=count`, and AC2 requires equal counts to be alphabetical. The demo catalog has three ties (11, 10 and 6 products) whose ids are not in name order (WildRunner id 3 before Raptor Elite id 6; Daybird id 1 before B&R id 5), so an ascending order, a missing tie-break or an id tie-break all fail. Functional runs the real ordered query in Postgres.

items.title: Summary with sort=name orders brands alphabetically
covers: AC4: sort=name orders the brands by name
items.reason: AC4 makes `name` an explicitly accepted value; a validator that only lets `count` through, or a switch that maps `name` to the count order, would break it. The ids are not in name order (id 1 is Daybird), so an unordered or id-ordered result fails. Functional is the cheapest layer with the real query.

items.title: Summary without sort keeps the alphabetical order
covers: AC4: name is the default when sort is absent
items.reason: AC4 says `name` is the default. Adding the parameter must not make it required (a missing value must not answer 400) nor change the BRAND-1 contract the page relies on. Functional, same endpoint as TC-BRAND-3-02, kept separate because "absent" and "name" go through different code paths.

items.title: Summary with an unknown sort value answers 400 with a problem naming name and count
covers: AC4: any other value answers 400
AC4: problem description names the allowed values
items.reason: AC4 requires any value other than `name` or `count` to be rejected with 400 and a problem description that names the allowed values, so a client learns how to fix the call. Without validation the endpoint would silently return some order. Functional checks the status code and problem body of the real endpoint.

items.title: Summary with an empty sort value answers 400
covers: AC4: any other value answers 400 (empty value)
items.reason: An empty `sort=` is the boundary between "parameter absent" (default name order, TC-BRAND-3-03) and "a value outside name and count" (400, AC4). Model binding can turn an empty string into null and silently treat it as the default; the literal reading of AC4 ("any other value") is a 400, as the as-built notes also decide. Functional checks the real binding.

items.title: Summary with sort=COUNT (different case) answers 400
covers: AC4: any other value answers 400 (case variant of an allowed value)
items.reason: AC4 accepts exactly `name` and `count`; `COUNT` is the closest value outside that set. The literal reading (and the as-built decision to match exactly) is a 400, so a case-insensitive comparison would be a contract drift between the API and the page, which also matches exactly. Functional checks the real validator. See Open questions in `_index.md`.

items.title: Brands page shows a Sort control with Name selected and cards in alphabetical order
covers: AC1: Sort control with Name and Most products
AC1: Name selected by default
AC1: cards in alphabetical order
items.reason: AC1 defines the page's initial state: a "Sort" control with exactly two options, "Name" selected, and the alphabetical order. A control that defaults to "Most products", or shows no selection, would fail. e2e because the control is rendered by the WebApp on the test stack.

items.title: Choosing "Most products" reorders the cards by count and adds ?sort=count to the address
covers: AC2: choosing Most products orders by number of products, largest first
AC2: equal counts in alphabetical order
AC2: address gets ?sort=count
items.reason: AC2 is the story's main user flow: the shopper picks "Most products", the cards reorder (largest count first, ties alphabetical) and the address records the choice. The demo ties (Gravitator / Raptor Elite / WildRunner at 11, B&R / Daybird at 10, AirStrider / Zephyr at 6) prove the page shows the API's tie order. e2e because it is a UI interaction through the WebApp and the API.

items.title: Reloading after choosing "Most products" keeps the count order
covers: AC2: a reload keeps the order
items.reason: AC2 says the choice survives a reload. If the order lived only in component state (not in the address), a reload would fall back to the name order. Separate from TC-BRAND-3-10 because here the page state comes from an in-page navigation followed by a browser reload. e2e because only the browser can reload.

items.title: Opening /brands?sort=count directly shows "Most products" selected and the count order
covers: AC3: opening /brands?sort=count directly selects Most products and shows that order
AC2: a shared link keeps the order
items.reason: AC3 (and the "shared link" part of AC2) requires the page to read `sort` from the address on first load in a fresh browser context, with no prior interaction. A page that only reorders on click would show the name order here. e2e because it covers the WebApp's query binding and its call to the API.

items.title: Opening /brands with an unknown sort value shows the alphabetical order with "Name" selected
covers: AC3: any other sort value shows the alphabetical order with Name selected
items.reason: AC3 says an unknown `sort` on the page is not an error: it falls back to the name order with "Name" selected. Since the API answers 400 for unknown values (AC4), a page that forwards the value unchanged would show an error instead of brands. e2e because it is the page's handling of its own address.

items.title: Opening /brands?sort=COUNT shows the alphabetical order with "Name" selected
covers: AC3: any other sort value (case variant of count) shows the alphabetical order with Name selected
items.reason: `COUNT` is the value closest to the accepted `count`; under the literal reading of AC3 it is "any other value" and falls back to the name order. It also guards against the page and API disagreeing on case (the page selecting "Most products" while the API answers 400, TC-BRAND-3-06). e2e because it is the page's handling of its own address. See Open questions in `_index.md`.

items.title: Choosing "Name" after "Most products" restores the alphabetical order
covers: AC1: Name option gives the alphabetical order
AC2: the address carries sort=count only for Most products
items.reason: The control has two options (AC1); switching back must work, not only the first switch. If the "Name" link kept `sort=count` in the address, the page would stay in count order. e2e because it is a UI interaction.
